score.prior_note_2026_08_27: First pass. Two evidence-grounded fixes found by reading the raw .s directly (not from the naive m2c/family-transplant seed, which m2c itself mis-scheduled in several places): (1) work->0x7784's stored value (0) is not a fresh literal at its point of use -- the reference materializes r2=0/movs r0,#0/mov sl,r2 immediately after storing `object` into work+0x7828 and before the Func_080cdb24 call, then reuses that same `sl` register for the field store roughly 40 instructions later. Introducing a `zero_val` local initialized at that exact point (matching the reference's early materialization) rather than writing a bare `0` literal at the field-store site dropped differing_halfwords 650->608 and wrong_instructions 572->546. (2) The scanline-table base pointer (`work+0x6980`) is computed by the reference immediately after the frame==65 check, before the amplitude range-check chain (frame<=31 / 47<frame<=63) -- not after it as the naive top-down reading suggested. Moving `scanline = (s32*)((u8*)work+0x6980);` to that earlier position (confirmed by re-reading the raw byte offsets around .L11 in games/gs1/asm/080cfef4.s) grew candidate_bytes 1352->1356 (closer to the 1396 target) and dropped wrong_instructions 546->534, though differing_halfwords rose slightly (608->642) from the resulting realignment -- the same 'small metric regression traded for real correctness' pattern documented on other siblings in this family, not a reason to revert.
score.residual: Ran a systematic same-opcode/same-register scan over the full candidate-show --align output specifically to separate genuine value/algorithm bugs from register-choice noise: zero matches found where the same instruction and same register hold different immediates on the two sides. Every remaining `!` line is either a differing register letter (candidate keeps a persistent loop value in r9 where the reference uses fp, mirroring the exact fp/r9 residual already recorded in games/gs1/recon/en/main/080d59b0.json for this same family) or a differing stack offset cascading from the still-unresolved 16-byte (4-word) frame-size gap (candidate sub sp #60 vs reference's #76). Tried moving pos[3]/idx_a/idx_b/member_object between block scope and function scope: zero effect on the emitted frame size or instruction stream, confirming (as the sibling dossiers already record for this same 0x03001eec family) that this compiler's stack-slot assignment for this owner is not controlled by C89 declaration nesting. Not pursued into open-ended register-forcing per the hard ban on hand-tuning register assignment; recorded as the same known-open class of residual documented across this family rather than chased further.

Semantic summary: a battle-presentation sub-effect keyed off the same *(void**)0x03001EEC work block as the member_orbit family. Loads two graphics resources (Value_000000ab as a palette+sprite pair, Value_000000ac copied straight into OBJ VRAM), sets BG2 affine scale and shear, opens two rectangle-blit routines (heap kinds 46/47), then runs a fixed 132-frame loop against one fixed party member (object+0x24). Each frame redraws a 160-entry per-scanline table (work+0x6980) from a sine sweep whose amplitude and offset change at several hardcoded frame boundaries (15/31, 32, 33, 47/63, 64, 65), and, once past frame 88, progressively reveals a run of glyph-style rectangles (increasing table offsets, six distinct width/height pairs) alongside a one-shot member-object field reset (frame 88) and a single field write (frame 120) -- most plausibly a spinning number or counter reveal effect.

Data_080ee10c/Data_080ee11a (two seven-byte-stride glyph-position tables at 0x080ee10c/0x080ee11a) and Data_03001e74 (an existing established `u8*` global, per games/gs1/recon/en/main/080ba978.c) are declared extern with no further semantic claim beyond what the raw offsets show.
No GS2 or external source was used; no other Golden Sun decompilation project was consulted.

compiler_decision.finding: The allocator decoder reports no unique source edit. Removing the redundant rectangle temporary, naming the callback literal, and swapping the screen-coordinate declaration order all emit identical bytes. -fno-regmove, canonical scheduling/CSE removals, and the neutral no-schedule/no-CSE axes preserve the 38-halfword floor; -fno-schedule-insns2, -fno-cse-skip-blocks, -ffixed-r6/r7, and -fcall-used-r6 regress by hundreds of halfwords, while -fcall-used-r7 is invalid for this target. No register binding or scheduling barrier was used.

decision: Retain the byte-exact structured assembly as a proven battle-effect compiler-allocation module. The complete named ordinary-C reconstruction accounts for all 1,396 owner bytes, which now count as DONE.
